variables.claim_asserts: The same freshwater fish species never occurs in the fresh waters of distant continents, although allied species may.
variables.test_measures: FishBase native or endemic country records for strictly freshwater, non-diadromous species shared across present-day ocean-separated continental landmasses, with six mechanically robust shared species.

modality.note: FishBase native-range and habitat records are an appropriate modality for species-level freshwater distributions, subject to acknowledged status and habitat coding errors.

assumptions.note: Ocean-separated present landmasses reasonably operationalize distant continents, but the registered threshold of five robust species is more demanding than Darwin's universal 'never,' for which one verified counterexample is sufficient.

scope.claim_scope: Freshwater fishes on distant continents, including the contrast between identical and allied species.
scope.test_scope: Strictly freshwater, non-diadromous FishBase species with native/endemic country records; the allied-species clause and brackish-tolerant freshwater fishes are not tested.

reasons: Cross-ocean native sharing of the same FishBase species directly measures the first clause of Darwin's assertion.
The interpretation explicitly narrows the analysis to strictly freshwater, non-diadromous records and does not test the allied-species clause.
Several mechanical matches are acknowledged habitat or occurrence-mode artefacts, so the species records require adjudication even though genuine Holarctic candidates remain.
what_would_change_it: Include all fishes occurring natively in fresh water under Darwin's usage, manually adjudicate native status and habitat for every counterexample, and separately test the allied-species clause.
